stage2.title: Prompt-Efficient Fine-Tuning for GPT-like Deep Models to Reduce Hallucination and to Improve Reproducibility in Scientific Text Generation Using Stochastic Optimisation Techniques
stage2.sentence: Through novel evaluation methods applied to LLMs, including BLEU, ROUGE, and Perplexity scores, the fine-tuned MS-GPT model demonstrated superior text coherence and reproducibility compared to the baseline GPT-2, confirmed through statistical analysis with the Wilcoxon rank-sum test.

stage2.title: Learning to vary: Teaching LMs to reproduce human linguistic variability in next-word prediction
stage2.sentence: We employ fine-tuning techniques for pre-trained and instruction-tuned models; and demonstrate their potential when fine-tuning GPT-2 and Mistral-7B-IT, using Provo Corpus.

stage2.title: The Automated LLM Speedrunning Benchmark: Reproducing NanoGPT Improvements
stage2.sentence: To evaluate the ability of AI agents to reproduce results in an active research area, we introduce the Automated LLM Speedrunning Benchmark, leveraging the research community contributions on the NanoGPT speedrun, a competition to train a GPT-2 model in the shortest time.

stage2.title: As Language Models Scale, Low-order Linear Depth Dynamics Emerge
stage2.sentence: Across tasks including toxicity, irony, hate speech and sentiment, a 32-dimensional linear surrogate reproduces the layerwise sensitivity profile of GPT-2-large with near-perfect agreement, capturing how the final output shifts under additive injections at each layer.

stage2.title: Generating In-store Customer Journeys from Scratch with GPT Architectures
stage2.sentence: Utilizing customer trajectory data, layout diagrams, and retail scanner data obtained from a retail store, we trained a GPT-2 architecture from scratch to generate indoor trajectories and purchase actions.

stage2.title: Reading Task Failure Off the Activations: A Sparse-Feature Audit of GPT-2 Small on Indirect Object Identification
stage2.sentence: We report a small, reproducible audit of which sparse-autoencoder (SAE) features of GPT-2 small fire differently on failed versus successful trials of the Indirect Object Identification (IOI) task.

stage2.title: On the Generalizability of "Competition of Mechanisms: Tracing How Language Models Handle Facts and Counterfactuals"
stage2.sentence: We reproduce their results on both GPT-2 (Radford et al., 2019) and Pythia 6.9B (Biderman et al., 2023).

stage2.title: Explaining Attention with Program Synthesis
stage2.sentence: We demonstrate that a set of fewer than 1,000 such generated programs can reproduce the attention patterns of heads in GPT-2, TinyLlama-1.1B, and Llama-3B, achieving an average Intersection-over-Union similarity above 75% on TinyStories.

stage2.title: Accelerating Reproducible Research in Synthetic EHR Generation
stage2.sentence: We reimplement and unify strong baselines (MedGAN, CorGAN, PromptEHR, HALO) under full ICD-9 vocabulary granularity, and add a lightweight GPT-2 baseline from the general-purpose sequence-modeling literature.

stage2.title: Low-rank Orthogonalization for Large-scale Matrix Optimization with Applications to Foundation Model Training
stage2.sentence: Numerical experiments demonstrate the superior performance of low-rank orthogonalization, with low-rank Muon achieving promising results in GPT-2 and LLaMA pretraining -- surpassing the carefully tuned vanilla Muon on tasks with large model sizes.

stage2.title: Mangosteen: An Open Thai Corpus for Language Model Pretraining
stage2.sentence: Systematic ablations using GPT-2 show the pipeline trims CommonCrawl from 202M to 25M documents while raising SEA-HELM NLG from 3 to 11; an 8B-parameter SEA-LION model continually pre-trained on Mangosteen then surpasses SEA-LION-v3 and Llama-3.1 by about four points on Thai benchmarks.

stage2.title: Heterogeneity in Formal Linguistic Competence of Language Models: Is Data the Real Bottleneck?
stage2.sentence: We pre-train simple GPT-2 Small (124M) models on a 100M-token random sample of the FineWeb corpus and intervene by injecting a minimal amount (1%) of synthetic data targeting specific linguistic phenomena.

stage2.title: Reproducibility Report: Test-Time Training on Nearest Neighbors for Large Language Models
stage2.sentence: Using pretrained RoBERTa embeddings indexed with Faiss, we retrieve 20 neighbors per test input and apply one gradient update per neighbor across GPT-2 (117M, 774M), GPT-Neo (1.3B), and R1-Distilled-Qwen2.5-1.5B.

stage2.title: One QK Channel, Many Sources: Guarding Low-Precision Attention Collapse
stage2.sentence: We isolate a reproduced GPT-2-class collapse to the streaming-softmax accumulator, where fp32 accumulation repairs it, and use the fault as an assay for moving controlled errors across sources.

stage2.title: mGPT: Few-Shot Learners Go Multilingual
stage2.sentence: We reproduce the GPT-3 architecture using GPT-2 sources and the sparse attention mechanism; Deepspeed and Megatron frameworks allow us to parallelize the training and inference steps effectively.

stage2.title: How Good Are LLMs at Out-of-Distribution Detection?
stage2.sentence: While existing research has probed OOD detection with relative small-scale Transformers like BERT, RoBERTa and GPT-2, the stark differences in scales, pre-training objectives, and inference paradigms call into question the applicability of these findings to LLMs.

stage2.title: Directional Optimization Asymmetry in Transformers: A Synthetic Stress Test
stage2.sentence: Excess loss above these floors reveals that even scratch-trained GPT-2 models exhibit a strong, reproducible directional optimization gap (e.g., 1.16 nats at K=5), far larger than that of an MLP trained on the same data.

stage2.title: SCIT: Testing Causal Cache Carriers in Latent Chain-of-Thought Models
stage2.sentence: On CODI-GPT2 and a Sim-CoT-style GPT-2 reproduction, counterfactual arithmetic transfers primarily through value-cache suffix trajectories rather than hidden states, keys, reusable answer slots, or single-token triggers.

stage2.title: The Newton-Muon Optimizer
stage2.sentence: Empirically, on a reproduction of the earliest publicly released Modded-NanoGPT speedrun configuration using Muon for GPT-2 pretraining, Newton-Muon reaches the target validation loss in 6\% fewer iteration steps and reduces wall-clock training time by about 4\%.

stage2.title: The Stability-Efficiency Dilemma: Investigating Sequence Length Warmup for Training GPT Models
stage2.sentence: To better understand this phenomenon, we conduct an in-depth analysis on large-scale pre-training experiments replicating the GPT-2 model.

hit.title: llm.c: reproducing GPT-2 (1558M)
hit.quote: reproduce this model on a single 8XH100 node in 24 hours, and for $672 ... we cross over the GPT-2 model around step ~25K [on HellaSwag]

adjudication.rationale: ⛔ THIS PROTOCOL DID NOT FIND IT -- not on arXiv, so the frame excluded it BY CONSTRUCTION. A round-2 reviewer found it. On the merits it is STRONGER than the RoBERTa hit: independent party, the EXACT scored size (1558M), a pretraining run from a corpus, a stated matching metric on HellaSwag, and published checkpoints. Scored 1 for the same reason. ⚠ Consistency required it: refusing it while accepting RoBERTa would be an adjudication chosen after seeing which way it cut, since it moves this release from BELOW two open-weights releases to LEVEL WITH them and weakens a confession the paper makes about its own error. ⚠ Both evidence urls are VOLATILE rendered pages; the digests are recorded but no digest of them is stable, which is itself why the cell caps at ASSERTED. Every stage-2 survivor was READ AT TITLE AND MATCHED-SENTENCE LEVEL, not in full text. An earlier draft said 'all were read', which overstates what the stored work supports; both round-2 reviewers said so independently. A third screen requiring the reproduction verb to fall within 25 characters of the model name is now IMPLEMENTED in negative_search.py and its records are stored per subject; it leaves 49 across the census. The figure of 33 that this field previously carried was never computed by anything and is not reproducible from the stored records. Each is one of: the paper USES the model, REPLICATES a finding or a result with it, or PRETRAINS A DIFFERENT MODEL -- frequently a domain-specific variant of the same architecture on a different corpus, which is not a reproduction of this release's training run.
